content.title: Masters 2026: How much are the caddies paid?
content.text: (NEXSTAR) – The 90th annual Masters is underway, with the infamous Par 3 contest and its celebrity caddies behind us. Now, all focus is on the chase for the tournament’s venerable green jacket, its multi-million dollar pot, and the white jumpsuit-clad caddies guiding the golfers to victory. Northern Ireland’s Rory McIlroy won the 89th Masters with a thrilling finish, completing a career Grand Slam and collecting a cool $4.1 million — the most in Masters history. As of Thursday, we don’t know how large the pot is this year, but it’s almost certainly expected to be above $4 million. What is also unknown is exactly how much the caddies will be paid this year. The estimates, however, could easily afford several dozen pimento cheese sandwiches. In most cases, a professional caddie collects a weekly paycheck from their player, in addition to a cut of the player’s winnings. Former PGA Tour caddie Michael Collins previously explained that, when it comes to tournaments like the Masters, the general rule is a “10-7-5” payout. “If the guy makes the cut, the standard is 10-7-5 — 10% for a win, 7% for a top 10, 5% for everything else,” Collins explained. Caddies may negotiate a lower tournament payout in exchange for a higher weekly paycheck, he noted. If McIlroy and his long-time caddie, Harry Diamond, followed that rule, Diamond may have collected roughly $410,000 for his work at the Masters last year. That’s far more than many of the top golfers secured at the tournament. Rory McIlroy, of Northern Ireland, is embraced by caddie Harry Diamond, left, after winning in a playoff against Justin Rose, of England, after the final round the Masters golf tournament, Sunday, April 13, 2025, in Augusta, Ga. (AP Photo/Matt Slocum) Diamond also gets to adorn his white jumpsuit with a special feature this year because of McIlroy’s victory. Caddies, while not taking the swings themselves, may also tap into some funds typically reserved for big-name athletes: sponsorship deals. Ted Scott, caddie for the victor of the 2024 Masters, Scottie Scheffler, recently told Golf Digest that caddies can, in fact, get sponsorship deals. He pointed to the PGA’s current partnership with Valspar. Scott explained that caddies can receive points for wearing Valspar-branded hats and based on how well their player does. At the end of the year, players are paid from a pool according to how many points they earned. Caddies for the top players may additionally receive part of their players’ sponsorship deals. That isn’t exactly raw profit for the caddie, though. They are usually responsible for their own expenses, like airfare, hotel, car rentals, food, and anything else that may pop up, Collins said during a 2021 episode of the “Green Light with Chris Long” podcast. Depending on the tour a caddie and golfer are on, those expenses could range from $25,000 to $50,000 a year, Michael Bestor, caddie for Kevin Streelman, previously explained. In addition to his hard-earned cash, the winning caddie can also ask to have the white jumpsuit they wore at the Masters sent their way after the tournament.
